semantics.note: The proposition joins two claims: a present claim that $358B is needed, and a firm conditional ('would be fatal') triggered by any growth slowdown. The wording and the antecedent are kept. The 2029 date qualifies the revenue figure, not the fatality clause.

contract.note: Reading 'fatal' as insolvency or cessation is a fair, ordinary reading. Applying the 2029 deadline to fatality, choosing the growth measure, and letting either company's slowdown count are evaluator choices that will decide the result. The contract flags these but marks interpretation_determines_result false.

evidence.note: Breakingviews (Oct 15-16, 2026) reports that Anthropic's Q3 growth slowed to 45%. This bears only on the antecedent. It shows neither the revenue necessity nor any business failure, so it is not evidence of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent (a growth slowdown) is plausibly met for Anthropic. The forecast runs to the end of 2029, after the evaluation date, and the packet has no conclusive event: no insolvency or cessation, and no validation or discharge of the $358B requirement. Continued operation does not settle the claim, so it stays unresolved.

contract.note: The plain reading (more than half of users, counted by head, refusing verified cost-covering prices) is ordinary and fair. The user population and the cost basis are evaluator choices that decide the result, and the contract says so.

evidence.note: YipitData's figures on business-customer retention at Anthropic (Oct 27, 2026) cover only sampled business customers. They do not establish that prices cover costs or represent all users, so they cannot settle the majority threshold.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet has no representative evidence of users accepting or refusing verified cost-covering prices. Business retention data is suggestive context only. Nothing meets the early-resolution rule, so the claim is unresolved.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to choose a discount trigger, a margin threshold, or a comparison period that the speaker did not supply, and treats the claim as not checkable.

evidence.note: ResultSense (Jul 31, 2026) reports OpenAI price cuts of 80% and 20% on some tiers. It gives no figures for inference margin or revenue, and the cuts cannot be matched to the speaker's unstated trigger.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent depends on an unspecified discount size, 'eaten alive' has no threshold, and the revenue clause is a rhetorical question. No unique test can be fixed from the words, so the claim is not adjudicable.
